title: A Big Thank You to Gator Fans For Their Juice — And Their Loyalty!
coverAlt: A Florida quarterback hands off to running back Jadan Baugh (No. 13) against Texas in Austin on Oct. 17, 2026. Photo courtesy UAA and Hannah White.
excerpt: Buddy Martin thanks Gator fans for their loyalty after Florida's 27-24 win at Texas and looks ahead to the open date. Photo courtesy UAA and Hannah White.
description: Buddy Martin thanks Gator fans for their loyalty after Florida's 27-24 win at Texas and looks ahead to the open date.

textCorrections.before: Down 7–3 at Texas, with untested backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. at the controls, Florida had an opportunity to follow a familiar and thoroughly unpleasant script.
textCorrections.after: Down 17-3 at Texas, with untested backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. at the controls, Florida had an opportunity to follow a familiar and thoroughly unpleasant script.

textCorrections.before: There’s still plenty to sort out over these last six games. I had this pegged as a 6–6 season, and these Gators are giving me reason to reconsider.

title: Gators find a spark in Austin
coverAlt: Florida defenders gang-tackle a Texas ball carrier in Austin on Oct. 17, 2026. Photo courtesy UAA and Hannah White.
excerpt: Eddie Gilley on Florida's 27-24 win at Texas: improved defense, third-down execution and the spark that helped the Gators fight back. Photo courtesy UAA and Hannah White.
description: Eddie Gilley on Florida's 27-24 win at Texas: improved defense, third-down execution and the spark that helped the Gators fight back.

textCorrections.before: The defense sucked a little less this week. They kept the Longhorns to less than 100 yards rushing, although that is deceitful in some ways because the total reflects 46 yards lost in sacks and TFLs. They held the highly publicized Arch Manning to 173 yards on 14 completions and sacked him 5 times including the fumble that sealed the win with 2 minutes left in the game. The biggest improvement was that they allowed the Texas offense to only make 2 of 10 third downs and only 1 of 3 fourth down attempts. The offensive line sucked less this week. They only gave up one sack to the nations leading pass rusher. Jaden Baugh finished with 91 yards rushing on 25 carries. He averaged 3.6 yards per carry and had one touchdown. The offense netted 158 yards on the ground and gained 184 yards before deducting 26 yards lost in the one sack, one bad snap, and TFLs. They gave Tramell Jones Jr. enough time to go 22-35 for a total of 155 yards and two touchdowns to Lacota Dippre. The offense found a way to score 27 points on the vaunted Texas defense led by Will Muschamp. That was the key to the Gators having a chance to win the game. They proved that they could keep drives alive going 8-19 on third downs, most of those coming in the second half and going 2-2 on fourth downs. The biggest one of those was the pass from Jones to Wilson from the Texas 36-yard line on a fourth and twelve play.

textCorrections.before: Because Florida sucked less this week, they have moved back into the top 25. There was a fire in the eyes of the Gator players that had been missing for the last two weeks. The game didn't start out well for the Gators. They didn't fold as they had in the previous two games. They fought back. They got off the deck, and they started landing punches of their own. The defense started to assert themselves up front. The offense looked like the balanced unit they need to be if they are going to be successful. Bailey Stockton found a way to return to the game when it looked like he was done for the day and maybe longer. Jaden Baugh looked like a man hungry to run through someone on every play again. Somewhere in the week leading up to the game or maybe at halftime they found a spark. We may never know what that spark was, was it something someone said or was it just a realization by the entire team that the game was right before them and all they needed to do was seize the moment.
